cards.text: Friend, this is Micah the Moreshite, a prophet carrying the word of the LORD about Samaria and Jerusalem (Micah 1:1). Now he cries 'Woe' to people who plot evil on their beds. Most of us lie awake replaying something awkward we said in a meeting, but these folks lie awake drafting a SCHEME.

cards.question: These people scheme on their beds. When morning's light comes, what do they do with the plan?

answers.text: They talk themselves out of it

cards.text: Micah says they can do it because the power is in their hands. That's the whole problem, friend: they CAN, so they DO.

cards.question: With all that power, these schemers covet ___ and seize them, and they take away houses.

cards.text: They push a man out of his home and take a fellow man's inheritance. Friend, that's not borrowing a coworker's stapler, that's taking what was meant to be passed down.
Then the LORD speaks. They've been lying in bed making plans, and uh-oh, now the LORD has plans too.

cards.question: The LORD says He's planning something against this nation. What is it?

answers.text: A warning they are free to ignore
A blessing on all their new land

cards.question: The LORD says that once this time of calamity comes, these people will keep walking just as proudly as before.

cards.text: In that day, people will take up a proverb against them and taunt them with a bitter lamentation. Picture the whole neighborhood singing your worst day right back at you.

cards.question: What does that bitter lament cry out?

cards.text: The lament says He has allotted our fields to traitors. Friend, the field-grabbers just got field-GRABBED.

cards.question: When the land is divided by lot, these people will still have someone in the assembly of the LORD to do it for them.

cards.text: Then somebody pushes back on the preaching: 'Do not preach,' they preach. Friend, that's like YELLING 'STOP YELLING' across the whole office.

cards.question: The ones saying not to preach these things are sure about something. What?

answers.text: The rains will come early this year
The king will reward their plans

cards.text: Then the LORD answers the house of Jacob. Should it really be said that the Spirit of the LORD is impatient, or that these are the things He does?

cards.question: The LORD says His words bring good to whoever holds the most power.

cards.text: His words bring good to the one who walks uprightly. But then the LORD says what His people have been doing lately.

cards.question: The LORD says that of late His people have risen up like ___.
The LORD says His people strip something off unsuspecting passersby. What is it?
The LORD says they drive the women of His people out of their pleasant homes.

cards.text: And they take the LORD's blessing away from their children. FOREVER, friend, and that word just sits there.

cards.question: Next comes an order: 'Arise and depart.' Why should they go?

answers.text: This is not their place of rest
A better land is waiting nearby

cards.text: This isn't their place of rest, because its defilement brings destruction. A grievous destruction.

cards.question: Picture a man of wind who lies and says he'll preach to them about wine and strong drink. How would this people take him?

answers.text: He'd be just the preacher for them
They'd run him right out of town
They'd ask the prophets to test him

cards.text: They don't want this preaching, but a windbag with a wine sermon gets a FRONT ROW seat. Then the tone flips, and the LORD says, 'I will surely gather all of you, O Jacob; I will collect the remnant of Israel.'

cards.question: The gathered remnant is brought together like ___ in a pen.
This gathered flock is described as a quiet, peaceful crowd.

cards.text: A noisy throng, like the dead batteries I shared that junk drawer with, all arguing over who had the most charge left! And the one who breaks open the way goes up before them.

cards.question: With someone breaking open the way ahead of them, they break through the ___ and go out by it.
As they go out, who passes through before them as their leader?

cards.text: Their King passes through before them, the LORD as their leader. Friend, I spent years shut in the dark, and when Someone opens the way out, you GO.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the next word of verse 2 ('fields'). No earlier card mentions land, so 'fields', 'flocks' and 'wells' are all equally likely. The baker can only guess the wording; there is no meaning to reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The setup rules out a wrong answer. Card 6's 'uh-oh, now the LORD has plans too' and the question's own 'planning something against this nation' both rule out 'A blessing on all their new land.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess the exact words of the lament ('We are utterly ruined'). Nothing on card 9 helps the baker choose it over 'Our wells have run dry' or 'Our walls have fallen down,' so the right pick comes down to luck.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The joke 'a windbag with a wine sermon gets a FRONT ROW seat' does not make sense. A preacher stands at the front; the listeners are the ones who sit in the front row. The image does not click right away and would need explaining.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Card 19 retells verse 13 and then says 'when Someone opens the way out.' The capital S makes 'Someone' the LORD, so the card treats the One who breaks open the way as the King. Verse 13 names them separately and never says they are the same.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
